service.description: The readiness checks the viewer may read (design §10 Health, §14): each registered provider whose required permission the viewer holds, called as the viewer, its answer read as checks with a state (ready, warning, failed, unavailable), a reason code, a message, the organization or store, the checked time, the freshness facet of a data source (watermark, expected frequency, lag; stale past its lag), the owner's fix link when the viewer opens it and the refresh registered for it when the viewer may run it. A provider that fails is named in failedProviders and shown unavailable, without its diagnostics, while the others answer; a provider the viewer cannot read is omitted, and an organization an owner refuses is left out. Narrowed by provider, owner app, Health group, organization (refused outside the viewer's scope, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE) and state. Admin Health, Home and Insights DataReadiness read it; it is exposed to the Assistant and MCP (admin_get_readiness).

Run a registered refresh operation (design §14) by its key: refused without the registration's own permission (REFRESH_DENIED), for a key not registered or naming a missing service (REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE) and for an organization outside the viewer's scope (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE). Calls the owner's service as the viewer with the organization, the operation key, the reason and only the scope parameters the registration names; never a service or index name from the request. Answers a safe result: requested, or failed when the owner's service fails.

Admin Home's summaries (design §3): Needs attention, the failing and warning readiness checks the viewer may read, worst first, each with its fix link when the viewer opens it; and the health cards, failed job runs and sign-in failures of the last day, unresolved system messages and backup coverage, each linking its list when the viewer opens it, a count that cannot be read shown unavailable. Refuses a user without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (PERMISSION_DENIED).

The readiness and support summary (design §16; impl-admin P19), the one projection of SupportSummary, its print and its redacted JSON: the instance (display name, framework version and package, when prepared and, unless redacted, by whom), the readiness checks the viewer may read (get#Readiness), the protocols' states (get#ProtocolReadiness) and the effective settings (get#EffectiveSettings, a secret only set or not), each section read with the viewer's own permissions and marked unavailable with its reason when refused. No environment, host facts, listeners, paths, users, fix links or diagnostics. Redacted also leaves out who prepared it and writes an email address as [address]. Refuses a user without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (PERMISSION_DENIED).

The settings index (design §7 SettingsHome, §14.2): the owners' registered settings landings the viewer may open, each shown only when its destination opens to the viewer's own groups and its view permission holds, with its owner, group (Company, Applications, Instance), scope, who configures it and a link to its readiness in Health when the viewer opens Health. Searched by text (title, description, owner, who configures), by owner app and by group. For an Admin user and for a BOSS user the settings index alone is granted to (impl-admin F46); refuses anyone else (ADMIN_UNAVAILABLE).

One of Admin's own readiness checks (design §3), the provider its registration names (admin.mailServer, admin.backup, admin.reportMail, admin.reportAlertTopic, admin.adminFactors, admin.jobRuns, admin.cluster, admin.telemetry), answering the readiness contract's checks; it reads the framework's own records and names no host, address or person. On a fresh instance the backup check warns that the nightly job is paused and that its mirror has no sendUrl (impl-admin F9). Refuses a user without ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW and an unknown check.
